APIKeyAuthenticationModel.description:
API key authentication.

Used by: Generic REST APIs, some cloud services. All fields are key references resolved from environment declarations.

api_key.description: Key reference for API key value

api_secret.description: Key reference for API secret (used alongside the API key)

endpoint.description: Key reference for API endpoint URL

header_name.description: Key reference for HTTP header name (default: 'X-API-Key')

AWSAuthenticationModel.description:
AWS access key authentication.

All fields are key references resolved from environment declarations.

access_key_id.description: Key reference for AWS access key ID

secret_access_key.description: Key reference for AWS secret access key

session_token.description: Key reference for AWS session token (temporary credentials)

role_arn.description: Key reference for AWS IAM role ARN for AssumeRole

AuthenticationModel.description:
How to authenticate to a cloud provider or an integration. `method` selects the scheme and the block of the same name holds its settings.

Credential fields are key references: the names of variables or secrets declared in an Environment, resolved when they are needed. Never put a credential value here.

Rules:
- The block named by `method` must be set (for example `method: oauth2` needs `oauth2`).
- No other method's block may be set at the same time.

ssh_key.description: SSH private key authentication (git deploy keys)

description.description: Human-readable description of this authentication configuration and setup instructions

CLIAuthenticationModel.description:
CLI-based authentication using local credentials.

Uses existing CLI authentication: az login, gcloud auth, aws configure. No credential references needed - uses ambient credentials.

use_cli.description: Use local CLI authentication (az, gcloud, aws)

CertificateAuthenticationModel.description:
Certificate-based authentication (mTLS).

All fields are key references resolved from environment declarations.

certificate_path.description: Key reference for client certificate file path

private_key_path.description: Key reference for private key file path

ca_bundle_path.description: Key reference for CA bundle file path

certificate_password.description: Key reference for certificate password (if encrypted)

GCPAuthenticationModel.description:
Google Cloud Platform service account authentication.

All fields are key references resolved from environment declarations.

project_id.description: Key reference for GCP project ID

credentials_json.description: Key reference for GCP service account JSON credentials (as string content)

credentials_file.description: Key reference for path to GCP service account JSON file

service_account_email.description: Key reference for GCP service account email

IntegrationEndpointsModel.description: A service endpoint address for a networked integration transport.

IntegrationLifecycleModel.description: Lifecycle hooks of an integration, keyed by phase name, for example `connect_before` or `teardown`. Accepted and validated, but strata does not run lifecycle hooks yet.

IntegrationLifecyclePhaseModel.description: One lifecycle phase: an optional description and the Python scripts it runs, as paths relative to the solution root. Only Python scripts are accepted for an integration.

scripts.description: Python script paths for this phase, relative to the solution root

IntegrationSpecModel.description:
What an external tool or service is and what it can do: its `type`, its `capabilities`, how to reach it and how to authenticate. Other documents bind to it by name, for example a provisioner, a remote, an audit sink, a security gate or a value store.

Rules:
- Every capability must be one of audit, container, features, image_findings, infrastructure, key_value, release_gate, scanner, secrets, sources, variables, or start with `x-`.
- `version` must be a constraint strata can parse, such as `~> 1.9` or `>= 1.17`.

type.description:
Type of the tool or service. Built-in types and the capabilities they provide:

- `terraform`: infrastructure. Runs Terraform.
- `opentofu`: infrastructure. Runs OpenTofu (`tofu`), for a provisioner with `tool: opentofu`.
- `compose`: container. Docker Compose.
- `helm`: container. Helm charts.
- `script`: infrastructure. Runs a script.
- `argocd`: infrastructure. Pushes rendered configuration to the git repository Argo CD watches.
- `flux`: infrastructure. Pushes rendered configuration to the git repository Flux watches.
- `git`: sources. Git credentials for remotes.
- `infisical`: variables, secrets. Infisical.
- `azure-keyvault`: secrets, key_value. Azure Key Vault.
- `azure-appconfig`: variables, features, key_value. Azure App Configuration.
- `azure-blob`: key_value. Records in Azure Blob Storage.
- `webhook`: audit. Posts audit events as JSON.
- `otel`: audit. Sends audit events as OpenTelemetry logs.
- `sentinel`: audit. Sends audit events to Microsoft Sentinel.
- `aikido`: release_gate, image_findings. The Aikido security platform.
- `trivy`: scanner. CVE scanner.
- `grype`: scanner. CVE scanner.
- `checkov`: scanner. Static IaC security scanner.

Any other type needs a plugin registered under the `strata.integrations` entry point group.

capabilities.description: What this integration provides. Core capabilities: `variables`, `secrets` and `features` (value stores), `key_value` (small keyed records with optional compare-and-swap), `infrastructure` (IaC and configuration tools such as terraform), `container` (Compose and Helm), `sources` (credentials for git, OCI and Helm remotes), `audit` (audit event destinations), `scanner` (security scanners), `release_gate` (pass/fail verdict for a repository at a commit) and `image_findings` (open issues for container images). A name starting with `x-` is a custom capability that strata does not dispatch on.

required.description: Whether this integration is required for platform operation

enabled.description: Whether this integration is enabled. A disabled integration is not auto-bound.

authentication.description:
Authentication configuration for accessing the integration

Rules:
- The block named by `method` must be set (for example `method: oauth2` needs `oauth2`).
- No other method's block may be set at the same time.

transport.description: How the integration is reached, for example `cli`, `http` or `sdk`. Omit to let the integration type choose. It is checked against the transports the type supports when the integration runs, not when the document is loaded.

version.description: Version constraint of the tool or service this integration expects, for example `~> 1.9` or `>= 1.17`. An assertion, not an installation: strata never installs software, so a mismatch fails the preflight check. A provisioner names an integration rather than stating its own version.

command.description: Overrides the integration class's default executable name. Needed for a generic/custom wrapper whose binary isn't known until the document supplies it; a built-in like terraform does not need this.

endpoints.description: Service endpoint, as `address` (a URL). Required by azure-keyvault, azure-appconfig, azure-blob, webhook, otel and sentinel; meaningless for CLI-only integrations such as terraform.

lifecycle.description: Hook scripts per phase name, Python only. Accepted and validated, but strata does not run lifecycle hooks yet.

configuration.description: Settings read by the integration's own type, not validated by strata. Known keys: `webhook`: `headers`, `token_env_var`, `auth_scheme`; `otel`: `resource_attributes`; `sentinel`: `data_collection_rule_id`, `stream_name`; `infisical`: `project_id`, `environment`; `aikido`: `region`, `release_gate`, `images`. Add an `attributeconfig` with `target.kind: integration` and `target.block: configuration` to validate them.

custom.description: Free-form values for your own scripts. Strata does not deliver them anywhere yet.

ManagedIdentityAuthenticationModel.description:
Managed/Workload Identity authentication.

Uses cloud provider managed identity (Azure MSI, GCP Workload Identity, AWS IAM Roles). No credential references needed - uses ambient credentials.

client_id.description: Key reference for user-assigned managed identity client ID (Azure only)

OAuth2AuthenticationModel.description:
OAuth2/OpenID Connect authentication.

Used by: Azure (Service Principal), generic OAuth2 providers. All fields are key references resolved from environment declarations.

client_id.description: Key reference for OAuth2 client/application ID

client_secret.description: Key reference for OAuth2 client secret

tenant_id.description: Key reference for tenant/directory ID (Azure AD, Okta, etc.)

token_url.description: Key reference for OAuth2 token endpoint URL

authorization_url.description: Key reference for OAuth2 authorization endpoint URL

SAMLAuthenticationModel.description:
SAML 2.0 authentication.

All fields are key references resolved from environment declarations.

idp_entity_id.description: Key reference for SAML Identity Provider entity ID

sp_entity_id.description: Key reference for SAML Service Provider entity ID

sso_url.description: Key reference for SAML Single Sign-On URL

certificate_path.description: Key reference for SAML certificate file path

SSHKeyAuthenticationModel.description: SSH private key authentication, used for git deploy keys. Every field is a key reference, never the key itself.

private_key.description: Key reference for the SSH private key (PEM/OpenSSH format)

passphrase.description: Key reference for the private key's passphrase, if encrypted

known_hosts.description: Key reference for a known_hosts entry pinning the remote host's key

TokenAuthenticationModel.description: Bearer or personal access token authentication, used for git over HTTPS. `token` is a key reference; `username` is a literal.

token.description: Key reference for the token/PAT value

username.description: Literal username to pair with the token — not a key reference

description: A connection to an external tool or service: Terraform, a secrets store, a git host, a scanner, an audit destination. Create one per tool or service and reference it by name where it is needed.

spec.description:
Integration specification (type, capabilities, authentication, ...)

Rules:
- Every capability must be one of audit, container, features, image_findings, infrastructure, key_value, release_gate, scanner, secrets, sources, variables, or start with `x-`.
- `version` must be a constraint strata can parse, such as `~> 1.9` or `>= 1.17`.
